newsitem.title: USA: GM to consolidate Michigan plants, invest $10.9 million.
newsitem.headline: GM to consolidate Michigan plants, invest $10.9 million.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said its Metal Fabricating Division will consolidate its headquarters from two Troy, Mich., locations to the Great Lakes Technology Centre in Flint, Mich., in late 1999 or early 2000.
The automaker also said it will invest about $10.9 million in its Flint, Mich., truck assembly plant, increasing its manufacturing flexibility and improving its focus on the truck market.
The $10.9 million is in addition to GM's $500 million investment in the facility previously announced in January.
"The consolidation brings about 1,000 jobs to Flint and strengthens the division's ability to be more competitive," said the world's largest automaker.
The Metal Fabricating Division employs 1,003 people at two buildings in Troy.

The division consists of 14 metal fabricating facilities -- six of which include die operations -- with additional responsibility for four contiguous stamping operations in Doraville, Ga.; Fairfax, Kans.; Oshawa. Ont.; and Wentzville, Mo.; and the Flint Tool and Die Shop.
Nationally, the division's 34,000 employees process an average of 1.7 million tons of steel for GM cars and trucks each year, the company said.

When improvements at the Flint truck plant are completed this fall, it will begin to assemble the 3500HD chassis cab, a product based on the current full-size C/K pickup, GM said. The plant currently builds Chevrolet and GMC full-size regular cab, extended cab, chassis cab and crew cab pickup trucks.
The plant's total production capacity will not increase with the addition of the 350OHD, nor will employment at Flint or GM's Janesville, Wis., assembly plant be affected.
GM's stock rose 37.5 cents to $55.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
